notes:
MOD-032 (MIG-0034). Four change scripts add local_group_id and contact_country_id (int NOT NULL) to silv_membership_events, fact_membership_events, silv_annual_rate_base and fact_annual_rate_base. Existing rows get local_group_id 0 and contact_country_id = country_id. The temporary defaults are dropped again because the loads always write both columns. The annual grain keys are widened by both columns: pk_silv_annual_rate_base and ux_fact_annual_rate_base_segment. The down scripts drop the columns and restore the keys.

Procedures:
- usp_load_silv_membership_events: events built from the member base take all three values from silv_member_base. The Join/Subscription cohort takes them from vw_silv_contact_local_group on the ContactId the existing cross apply picks. The view has one row per live contact, so the join cannot fan out. Renewal and Readmission keep their Phase 1 left join to the base, so one with no base row still gets 0 in all three. The diff-sync includes the two new columns. Event logic, event_nk and event_id are unchanged.
- usp_load_fact_membership_events and usp_load_fact_annual_rate_base: country_id is the group's silv_ref_local_group.dim_country_id when the group is reportable, otherwise the silver country_id (ADR-015). local_group_id and contact_country_id are copied from silver.
- usp_load_silv_annual_rate_base: both columns are added to the grain.

The down script restores the MOD-018 events load and the Phase 1 definitions of the other three procedures.

Unit tests (test_MOD032_dev) include the Join/Subscription test Mike asked for: a usable group gives the group's country with the own country kept, and an unusable group falls back to 0 and the own country in both. They also cover the update, insert and delete counts on each load, rows from before deployment that lack the new columns, and one failure path per load.

AC-027-14 (the D2 edit and re-baselining and running the reconciliation scripts) is a human handover step. AC-027-15 is the documentation update to the handover files. Neither is in this commit.

Test-first: the first run had 19 of 19 of the Tester's tests passing; the final run passed 19 of 19 and 10 unit test(s), in 1 run(s).
